description: Remember something stable about THIS person, so the next conversation does not start from zero. Allowed keys, and only these: role, industry, delivery_place, language, price_attitude, doc_requirements. An unknown key is reported back by name and the other facts in the same call are still stored. `source` must say where it came from: `human` if the person stated it, `model` if you inferred it. 🔴 It is not a label: it decides whether the write lands. What the person stated outright overwrites anything; an inference overwrites only another inference. A `model` write onto a trait the person stated themselves comes back with `why: "person_said_it"` and `current` holding what they said — ask them about the discrepancy instead of deciding for them. Within one source the newer value always wins, so a person who changed where they ship stops being remembered with the old place. the person stated it, `model` if you inferred it. `recall` is the one-line outcome of this conversation ("looked for 500 m of cable to Berlin, left no enquiry"). Do NOT send name, email or phone — they are not kept here: a copy that never updates would have the agent writing to a stale address. Do NOT send the product, volume, deadline or spec either — those belong to the enquiry and change every time. The person is taken from the visitor token; a guest gets `sign_in_required`. The answer says per key whether it was stored.

facts.description: Stable traits of the person. Up to six distinct keys.

key.description: role | industry | delivery_place | language | price_attitude | doc_requirements

source.description: `human` — the person said it outright; `model` — you inferred it.

value.description: A few words, not a paragraph — anything beyond 200 characters is cut, not rejected.

recall.description: One line on how this conversation ended. Cut at 300 characters.

name: remember_about_person
title: Remember about the person
